title: Information Cascades in the Laboratory

studies.implementation_scope: The runtime includes three baseline sessions and the two public-draw sessions whose timing is specified. The reported aggregate findings pool all six symmetric sessions, including one under-described public-draw session that is not implemented.

findings.main_hypothesis: Participants follow a rational cascade when public evidence dominates a conflicting private signal.
Participants use public information efficiently rather than relying only on their private draw.
When the posterior is tied, participants generally follow their private signal rather than the preceding public prediction.

studies.implementation_scope: Published sessions 4 and 5 are implemented because the article specifies exactly when and to whom the two public draws were revealed.

findings.main_hypothesis: Decision makers continue to use Bayesian posterior information when a three-draw sample is representative of the lower-posterior urn.

studies.implementation_scope: All six reported asymmetric sessions are implemented using the urn compositions and common 15-period sequential procedure specified in the article.

findings.main_hypothesis: Information cascades remain prevalent when light and dark signals have unequal informativeness.
When Bayesian updating and simple signal counting disagree, participants choose the Bayesian prediction about half of the time.
Counting explains a substantial subset, but not all, of the asymmetric treatment's deviations from Bayesian choice.

required_tests.description: Every paid response is a valid A/B prediction.
Every executed session contains six ordered decisions in each of 15 paid periods.
Each decision maker sees exactly the predictions announced before their position.
The current private signal is available at decision time and the selected urn is revealed after the period.
Each correct prediction earns $2 and each incorrect prediction earns $0.
Every decision maker receives the complete rules and public practice transcript before their first paid prediction.
Practice continues until both urns appear, all draws are public, and no practice prediction or payoff is produced.
Executed sessions follow the evidence-complete prefix of the published treatment schedule and use the correct urn compositions.
Only positions 5 and 6 in published sessions 4 and 5 see the same two public draws introduced after prediction 4.

source_limitations: The paper states that a complete data appendix was available from the authors on request; it is not included in the public PDF.
The article reports three symmetric sessions with public draws but specifies the insertion of two draws after the fourth prediction only for sessions 4 and 5.
The unspecified public-draw session is omitted, leaving 66 implemented decision makers across 11 sessions rather than the reported 72 across 12 sessions.
Participant-level original decisions are unavailable, but those decisions are not required to recreate the randomized experimental environment and information timing.
